actuatorlist: compare robot actuators by torque, weight and price

actuatorlist is an independent, open catalog of the actuators that move robots: quasi-direct-drive motors, integrated joints, smart servos, harmonic and cycloidal reducers, and frameless motor kits. It holds 68 actuators from 30 brands in 6 categories, plus 6 robots with the motor in each joint. Robot builders use it to shortlist actuators for quadruped legs, humanoid joints and robot arms by the numbers that decide a build: peak torque, weight, torque density and price.

Browse the catalog

  • Leaderboard: torque density rankings and a torque versus cost scatter.
  • All actuators: every entry in one sortable table.
  • Actuator gallery: photos and spec cards by category.
  • Robots: which motors sit in each joint of real robots.
  • For AI agents: REST API, MCP server and markdown views.

Actuator categories

  • QDD / Proprioceptive (10): Quasi-direct-drive motors with low gear ratios; backdrivable, used in legged robots.
  • Integrated Joint (12): Motor, gearbox, encoder and driver in one housing, sized for arm and humanoid joints.
  • Smart Servo (15): Compact bus servos with onboard control, common in hobby and research arms.
  • Harmonic / Precision (9): Strain-wave (harmonic) gearing with near-zero backlash for precise positioning.
  • Frameless + Driver (14): Frameless motor kits and standalone motor drivers for custom actuator builds.
  • Cycloidal / Premium (8): Cycloidal and RV reducers for high-torque, shock-tolerant industrial joints.

Frequently asked questions

What is actuatorlist?

A free, open directory of robot actuators: 68 actuators from 30 brands in 6 categories, plus 6 robots with the motor in each joint. Every entry lists peak and rated torque, weight, torque density, price where public, and the sources the numbers came from.

Which actuators suit a quadruped leg?

Usually quasi-direct-drive (QDD) motors or low-ratio integrated joints, because they are backdrivable and survive impacts. Among entries tagged for quadruped legs, the highest torque density belongs to M107 Joint Motor (Unitree Robotics), RobStride 04 (RobStride), GIM6010-36 (48V) (Steadywin).

Which actuators suit a humanoid joint?

Integrated joints and QDD motors with enough peak torque for hips and knees. Among entries tagged for humanoid joints, the highest torque density belongs to M107 Joint Motor (Unitree Robotics), RMD-X8-120 (MyActuator), RobStride 04 (RobStride).

Which actuators give the most torque per dollar?

Among entries with a public USD price, the lowest price per Nm of peak torque belongs to RobStride 04 (RobStride), DM-J10010-2EC (DAMIAO (DMBots)), RobStride 03 (RobStride).

How reliable are the specs?

Each entry links its sources. Entries marked verified were spot-checked against manufacturer pages or datasheets; the rest are flagged unverified. Confirm critical numbers against the datasheet before you buy.

Do I need an account or API key?

No. The site, the REST API at https://actuatorlist.com/api and the MCP server at https://actuatorlist.com/mcp are public and read-only. There are no accounts, no keys and no fees.

How do I add or correct an actuator?

Open an issue or a pull request on GitHub at https://github.com/Miyamura80/getactuators. The dataset lives in the repository and is published under the MIT License.
